issue.title: [bug] decide= on a plugin provider (commandcode-plan) reports saved but never persists — Command Code Jev unreachable without a custom-provider detour
issue.body:
## Problem

`magpie provider set commandcode-plan decide=…` prints `✓ saved`, but the field is dropped immediately: the provider entry in providers.json has no `decide`, `magpie provider commandcode-plan` doesn't show it, and `POST /v1/systemone` with `commandcode-plan/typesafe/jev` answers:

```
magpie knows no Jev model "commandcode-plan/typesafe/jev"; name the provider before it, like openrouter/typesafe/jev-1.14
```

Meanwhile a group member on the plan provider gets plain chat completions, which Command Code's chat endpoint refuses:

```
Command Code Plan: Model "typesafe/jev" is not supported on this endpoint.
```

So a decision group can never reach Command Code's Jev through the plan provider.

## Command Code does serve Jev (verified against the live API)

- `POST https://api.commandcode.ai/provider/v1/systemone`, TypeSafe SystemOne body (`state` + `questions` + `model`), key in `Authorization: Bearer` and `x-api-key`.
- The endpoint's own validation names its models — sending `model: "garbage/vendor-xyz"` returns:

```
Model "garbage/vendor-xyz" is not supported on this endpoint. Use one of: typesafe/jev, typesafe/jev-1.14.0.
```

- The provider's `/provider/v1/models` list (92 models) does not include them, so catalog fetches never reveal Jev.
- On a GOAT account the call currently ends `insufficient credits` (Jev draws from credits, not the plan's usage windows), but route and model validation pass — the wiring is the only gap.

## Workaround (works end-to-end on 0.1.1309)

```
magpie provider add cc-jev decide=https://api.commandcode.ai/provider/v1 key=<commandcode key> models=typesafe/jev
magpie group add Jev id=jev models=cc-jev/typesafe/jev routing=order
# POST /v1/systemone model=group/jev → reaches the endpoint, fails only on the account's credits
```

Note `decide=` must be the base (`…/provider/v1`); magpie appends `/systemone`.

## Expected

Either keep the k=v fields (`decide`, `url`, …) set on plugin-managed providers, or have the commandcode plugin declare its System One endpoint and the plan's Jev model so `commandcode-plan/typesafe/jev` works directly.

## Version

magpie 0.1.1309, macOS arm64

comments.body:
## Update — 2026-10-24: corrected delivery after independent review

My original `b2497dd8` / `007b8b9b` delivery was incomplete: saving `decide=` alone did not demonstrate that the plugin's unlisted Jev could be discovered and routed. Review also found provider-identity regressions.

The current delivery is [`r3-batch`](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/r3-batch), fixed head [`7f927133be68a452f662d0c7445a1432e66c426a`](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/7f927133be68a452f662d0c7445a1432e66c426a), based on `b437e4adb4dba82446e0d625b040a8e2d95004b4`. It supersedes the earlier batch branches. This is the complete tested tree; `7f927133` itself is only the final identity correction, not a standalone fix for this issue.

The corrected behavior is:

- `decide=` survives saving and re-reading without replacing the plugin account or changing its public provider ID. A plugin's declared endpoint remains when the user sets no override.
- An explicitly selected decision-shaped model such as `typesafe/jev` is discoverable through `Deciders`/`OfferedDeciders` and the editor's `DecisionModels` metadata, and resolves through `RouteDecider`. It supplies the default when the plugin lists no decision model; an existing plugin-declared decision default keeps its priority. Ordinary selected chat models remain chat models.
- Saved settings survive sign-out under the plugin's actual public ID. Independent providers, including nameless/keyless local decision servers and an unused `cline-plugin` ID, remain visible. The final correction excludes raw account `decide=` settings from the stored-endpoint test used to claim a `-plugin` alias, matching `PluginID`/`customIDs`.

[`TestPluginPickedDecisionModelRoutes`](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/blob/7f927133be68a452f662d0c7445a1432e66c426a/internal/gateway/plugin_decide_picked_test.go) uses a plugin fixture whose feed contains chat models but no Jev. It covers save → re-read → stable identity → discovery/default → `RouteDecider` → `POST /v1/systemone`, and checks the stub receives `/provider/v1/systemone`, model `typesafe/jev`, and Bearer authentication. The final raw-picks/unused-alias regression and the identity/sign-out/default controls are included in the delivered tests.

These are local fixture/transport and editor-metadata checks. I have not tested the real Command Code service or driven the native GUI; the live endpoint observations remain yours. General subscription endpoint overrides are outside this change.

The [delivery ledger](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/blob/c1e0d235ed309438795fc07c86d7d04c3132c44b/docs/fork/upstream-status.json) records the ordered history and previous heads. The batch includes other fixes; its full 26-commit history is not a request to pick unrelated changes, and I am not claiming a selectively extracted subset was independently tested. The [final verification manifest](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/blob/c1e0d235ed309438795fc07c86d7d04c3132c44b/docs/fork/evidence/round7/manifest.json) records 66 packages passing, three tracked failures (#3280, #2207, #3284), and 19 no-test packages; the full suite exited 1.

AI-assisted implementation and review. The original delivery text below is retained as superseded history.

---

<details>
<summary>Original delivery text (superseded; retained for traceability)</summary>

Published a fix in my fork: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/b2497dd8 (branch [`fix/issue-batch-1023pm`](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/issue-batch-1023pm), based on current main). It takes the first half of your Expected — the k=v `decide` field now sticks on plugin-managed (and any signed-in) providers.

## Root cause, confirmed exactly as you narrowed it

`provider set` finds the provider through `All()`, where a signed-in provider is the **account** provider with the user's picks applied (`withPicks`), and `provider.Save` for an account id writes back only a whitelisted picks record — the whitelist (`internal/provider/provider.go`, the `p = Provider{ID: …, Models: …, RestCap: …}` line) had no `Decide`, so the field was silently dropped while the CLI printed "✓ saved". `withPicks` didn't carry it either, so even a hand-written entry wouldn't have reached the live provider.

## The fix, three pieces on one path

1. **Save's account whitelist keeps `Decide`** beside the queue/rests fields it already keeps;
2. **`withPicks` carries it** onto the account in `All` and onto every account in `AlsoOn` (same as the queue settings, #1899) — so `magpie provider set commandcode-plan decide=https://api.commandcode.ai/provider/v1 models=typesafe/jev` now works, and `/v1/systemone` with `commandcode-plan/typesafe/jev` resolves;
3. **a stored entry whose id is an account's stays that account's picks** even though `hasEndpoint` counts a decision API — without this, the saved decide-bearing entry would have stood in front of the sign-in and hidden it. This one only matters once (1) exists, but it fails visibly without it.

## Verification

`TestAccountKeepsItsDecide` (a signed-in account standing in for the plugin, your URL byte for byte) fails three ways with each piece reverted alone — `the account's decide: ""` (whitelist; withPicks) and `the stored decide entry stood in for the sign-in` (classification) — and passes with all three. Whole `internal/provider` package passes; gofmt clean; `go vet ./internal/provider` ok. The live-API half (endpoint validation, the credits answer) is your own verification, which this builds on.

Not covered here, deliberately: `url=`/endpoint overrides on subscription providers stay dropped — the plugin owns those, and overriding them is a bigger question than this issue's demonstrated gap.

</details>

**Update — 2026-10-24:** this was an intermediate follow-up. The corrected delivery, including plugin identity, explicit Jev discovery/routing and subsequent regression fixes, is documented in the [updated main delivery comment](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/3349#issuecomment-6364310053). Current tested tree: [`r3-batch` at `7f927133`](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/7f927133be68a452f662d0c7445a1432e66c426a). The old `007b8b9b` link below is retained as history.

---

<details>
<summary>Original delivery text (superseded; retained for traceability)</summary>

Follow-up on the same branch: [007b8b9b](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/007b8b9b) — `withPicks` was taking `pk.Decide` unconditionally, which would have wiped a plugin's *own* declared System One endpoint (a gateway test with a declare-decide plugin caught it). The pick now names the endpoint only when it has one; `TestAccountKeepsItsDecide` and the plugin decide tests pass.

</details>

## Result

I independently verified the `decide=` persistence part of vincent's earlier patch. This is not a claim that those two commits fully resolve #3349, and it does not supersede skygunner's later `r3-batch` delivery.

Original commits: `b2497dd82f46fe1279867aa42b2b4769d213c377`, `007b8b9b7433bc2b7f452f9526ed698a8aa2b49f`  
Rebased verification branch: [`verify/issue-3349-decide`](https://github.com/Edward4226/magpie/tree/verify/issue-3349-decide)  
Head: `6cf19e631ce898a4d733cb44f5b1a853e15e7de2`  
Base: `20d63621d12c137986b4ba86a3fa3d7873fcb95a` (`origin/main`)

## Verified behavior

- `decide=` survives provider save and re-read on a signed-in/plugin-managed provider.
- A plugin-declared System One endpoint is not replaced when the user did not set one.
- An explicit `decide=` routes through the plugin's System One path.

## Evidence

Using an isolated Bun 1.4.4 on Windows x64, both of these passed five consecutive runs after the rebase:

```text
go test -tags nogui ./internal/provider -run '^TestAccountKeepsItsDecide$' -count=5 -v
go test -tags nogui ./internal/gateway -run '^TestPluginServesSystemOne$' -count=5 -v
```

`TestPluginServesSystemOne` printed five explicit `PASS` results rather than being skipped. The mutation check is real: making `withPicks` assign `a.Decide = pk.Decide` unconditionally fails `TestAccountKeepsItsDecide` with `the account's decide: ""`; restoring it passes. `gofmt`, `git diff --check`, and `go vet` / `go build` with `-tags nogui` passed on the host, Linux, and Windows targets.

## Boundaries and gaps

- This branch covers only the earlier persistence/endpoint-preservation layer. It does not include skygunner's later Jev discovery and routing work, so it must not be presented as the complete #3349 fix.
- Not tried: a real Command Code Jev key, request, or credits response.
- Not tried: the GUI provider-edit or migration flow.
- Not tried: the complete suite or `-race`; this machine has no `gcc`.

## Action

Treat this as supporting evidence for the `decide=` layer, not as a competing delivery. Please review skygunner's current `r3-batch` tree for the complete behavior and preserve vincent's authorship on these two commits if they are reused.

issue.title: [bug] 插件供应商的「价格倍率」保存后没有持久化，计费仍按官方价

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## 问题

供应商插件（OpenCode 兼容）提供的供应商，在编辑页「高级 → 价格倍率」里填写并保存后，倍率没有被保存：重新打开编辑页时输入框是空的，`providers.json` 里也没有 `priceRate`，用量仍按官方价格计费。同样的操作对自定义供应商正常生效。

## 复现

1. 准备一个最小的供应商插件：

   `package.json`

   ```json
   { "name": "rate-repro", "version": "0.0.0", "type": "module", "main": "./index.js" }
   ```

   `index.js`

   ```js
   export default async () => ({
     config: async (cfg) => {
       cfg.provider ??= {};
       cfg.provider["rate-repro"] ??= {
         name: "Rate Repro",
         npm: "@ai-sdk/openai",
         api: "http://127.0.0.1:9/v1",
         models: { "gpt-5": { name: "gpt-5" } },
       };
     },
     auth: { provider: "rate-repro", methods: [{ type: "api", label: "API key" }] },
   });
   ```

2. 安装并登录，再添加一个自定义供应商作对照：

   ```bash
   magpie plugin add ./rate-repro
   magpie plugin login rate-repro          # key 任意
   magpie provider add ctl url=http://127.0.0.1:9/v1 responses=http://127.0.0.1:9/v1 key=x
   magpie provider models ctl gpt-5
   ```

3. 分别打开「供应商 → Rate Repro」和「供应商 → ctl」，在「高级 → 价格倍率」填 `0.15` 并保存。
4. 重新打开两个编辑页，再执行 `magpie model price rate-repro/gpt-5` 和 `magpie model price ctl/gpt-5`。

## 实际结果

| | 发给 `provider/save` 的请求体 | 重新打开后的输入框 | `providers.json` | `magpie model price` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 插件供应商 `rate-repro` | `priceRate: 0.15` | 空 | 没有 `priceRate` | `$1.25/$10`（官方价） |
| 自定义供应商 `ctl` | `priceRate: 0.15` | `0.15` | `priceRate: 0.15` | `$0.1875/$1.5`（× 0.15） |

前端两次都把 `priceRate` 发给了 `provider/save`，保存也提示成功；但对插件供应商，这个值没有被写入，计价也没有应用。

## 预期结果

插件供应商的价格倍率和自定义供应商一样被保存，并在计价时生效。如果插件供应商不支持价格倍率，编辑页不应显示这个输入框，或者保存时应给出提示。

## 影响

经插件接入的中转往往按官方价的一定倍率计费。现在只能逐个模型手动设置价格，例如 `magpie model price <provider>/<model> <in>,<out>,<cache read>,<cache write>`，上游调价后还要逐个同步。

## 相关

- #3349：插件供应商上的 `decide=` 同样显示已保存但没有持久化，可能是同一处原因（`provider/save` 对插件供应商只保留部分字段）。
- #3038：让插件声明自己的价格。即使合入，倍率仍需要能保存在插件供应商上（该 Issue 的方案中写的是 "the provider's price rate still applies"）。

## 环境

- magpie 0.1.1418
- macOS 27.2，arm64
- 在隔离的 `HOME` 下复现，通过 `magpie web` 的供应商编辑页操作。桌面应用里的插件供应商也是同样情况：修改价格倍率后再打开编辑页，输入框为空，计费没有变化。

issue.title: cli: `provider set` on a signed-in account says saved for pairs Save drops

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
`magpie provider set <id> k=v` on a signed-in account or a plugin's
provider runs every pair through `applyPairs`, then `provider.Save`, and
prints "✓ saved". For an account, Save keeps only what `withPicks` puts
back on it (#3743), so these pairs are dropped without a word:

`name=`, `icon=`, `catalog=`, `website=`, `url=` (`chat=`, `openai=`),
`responses=`, `anthropic=`, `gemini=`, `decide=`, `key=` (Kiro's is
kept), `keys=`, `balance=`, `balance.path=`, `balance.method=`,
`balance.token=`, `access.key=`, `access.secret=`, `models.url=`,
`codex=`, `search=`, `unmasked=` and `header.<Name>=`.

Each is a field an account doesn't take, and why is written down in
`accountApart` (internal/provider/account_picks_test.go, from the #3743
fix). Today only `user-agent=` is refused for an account (`applyPairs`:
"signs in as its own client"), and Vertex's `project=` and the presets'
`region=`/`plan=` are refused because an account isn't one.

`decide=` on a plugin's provider is #3349, which has patches of its
own; the other pairs have no issue.

Read from the code (internal/cli/providers_cli.go `set`, `applyPairs`;
internal/provider/provider.go `Save`), not run.

What would fix it: `applyPairs` refuses each of these for `p.Account !=
nil` with the reason `accountApart` gives, as it does `user-agent=`, and
a test sets every pair on a signed-in account and expects each one
either kept (read back through `provider.Find`) or refused.

issue.title: [bug] plugin provider: decide: true blocks model fetch before the first list is loaded

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Summary

A plugin provider that declares `decide: true` cannot fetch its ordinary model list before the first provider listing has populated any model endpoints. Magpie temporarily sees the provider as decision-only and sends the model refresh to `fetchDecide`, which fails with:

```text
HMind's plugin lists no decision models
```

After restarting Magpie, the previously saved model list is loaded and the same action works. A plugin cannot avoid this race by dynamically declaring `decide`, because provider-level `decide` can only be set from the `config` hook, which runs once when the plugin host loads.

## Environment

- macOS arm64
- Magpie `0.1.3295` (the same ordering is still present on `main`)
- `@hmind/magpie-hmind-provider` `0.1.1`

## Reproduction

1. Install and sign in to the HMind plugin.
2. Before Magpie completes its first model listing, open the HMind provider and click **Fetch models**.
3. Magpie reports `HMind's plugin lists no decision models` and the provider's model list remains empty.
4. Restart Magpie. The saved list loads and the provider works normally.

I reproduced this in an isolated HOME with a fake API key and a mocked `provider.models` response containing two ordinary chat models:

```text
immediately after sign-in: models=0 decideOnly=true decideModels=0
Fetch models immediately after sign-in: HMind's plugin lists no decision models
after the list is available: models=2 decideOnly=false decideModels=0
```

No real HMind request or real Magpie configuration was used in that reproduction.

## Root cause

The plugin declares the provider and models in the normal supported way:

- `config` sets `decide: true` on the provider.
- `provider.models` dynamically lists chat models and marks only real decision models with `decides: true`.

At startup, `host.js` runs the `config` hook once and records `decide: true`, but no model endpoints have been discovered yet. `pluginProvider` therefore creates a provider with `Decide` set and no `Chat`/`Responses` endpoint.

Two paths then take the decision-only branch too early:

1. `Provider.fetchList` checks `p.DecideOnly()` before `p.Account.fetch`:

   `internal/provider/models.go`

   ```go
   if p.DecideOnly() {
       return p.fetchDecide(ctx)
   }
   if p.Account != nil && p.Account.fetch != nil {
       return p.Account.fetch(ctx)
   }
   ```

2. `Provider.Test` immediately returns `p.testDecide(ctx)` when `p.DecideOnly()` is true:

   `internal/provider/test.go`

   ```go
   if p.DecideOnly() {
       return p.testDecide(ctx)
   }
   ```

For a plugin, `fetchDecide` uses the models already marked by the provider. Since no model list has loaded, that set is empty and it returns `"<name>'s plugin lists no decision models"`.

This is a transient host-state bug, not a missing upstream model and not a network failure. `decide: true` declares an additional API; it does not mean every model is a decision model.

## Expected behavior

- Fetching a plugin's model list should first ask the plugin's account model list, even if the provider currently looks decision-only.
- A provider test should not enter `testDecide` when the current plugin listing contains no decision model.
- After refreshing the list, the provider should be re-read so its newly discovered conversation endpoints can be tested normally.

## Suggested fix

1. In `fetchList`, prefer `p.Account.fetch` before the `DecideOnly` fallback.
2. In `Test`, require at least one current decision model before the early `testDecide` return; otherwise fetch the list, re-read the provider, and continue with ordinary model/endpoint tests.

The second point matters because fixing only `fetchList` makes **Fetch models** work but leaves **Test** able to emit the same decision-model error on the same initial state.

This is related to, but distinct from, #3349. #3349 concerns persisting a user-provided `decide=` override. This issue concerns the host classifying a plugin as decision-only before its first model list exists.
